intro_html: Nigiri is pressed, not packed: the outside holds, the inside stays loose enough to fall apart in your mouth. The pictures are close-ups of which finger does what, for a right-handed cook — the left hand holds the fish and cups the piece, the right hand shapes the rice and does the pressing. Start with sushi rice at about body temperature. Practise a few rice-only pieces first.

notes.html:
• Swap every hand: fish in the right hand, rice and pressing with the left.
  • The Japanese Food Lab's original instructions are written that way.

• These are home-size pieces, 15–20 g of rice (Umami Cart's guide).
  • At an Edomae counter a piece is smaller — around 10 g, so the fish wraps it almost completely.

• Too hard and the rice turns dense and gummy; too soft and it falls apart on the way to the soy.
  • Each press is light — a few small squeezes, not one big one.

• Buy fish sold for raw eating and keep it cold until you slice it.
  • Salmon for sushi should have been frozen first.
  • Eat nigiri the day it's made.

• The order of moves is the Japanese Food Lab's kote-gaeshi (written for a left-hander), mirrored for a right hand and checked against Sushi University's description.
  • The hand drawings are schematic — the point is which finger goes where.

steps.body_html:
• Mix the water and rice vinegar in a small bowl.
  • Dip just your fingertips and rub the water over both palms. Damp, not dripping: too wet and the rice slides, too dry and it sticks. Re-wet before every piece.

steps.title: Tezu: wet your fingertips

steps.body_html:
• Find the grain (the faint white lines) and cut across it.
  • Tilt the knife 30–45°, set the heel on the far edge and draw it towards you in one long pull — don't saw.
  • Aim for slices about 6–7 cm long, 2.5–3 cm wide and 3–5 mm thick, about 12–14 g each.

  • Hold it like an egg — no squeezing yet.

• Lay a slice of fish across the fingers of your left hand, around the middle joints, with your left thumb resting at the base of the index finger.
  • With your right index finger, dab a pea of wasabi in the middle of the fish.

steps.title: Left hand: the fish, then wasabi

steps.body_html:
• Set the rice on the fish.
  • Left thumb: press a small dimple into the middle of the rice — it keeps the inside loose.
  • Right thumb and index finger: squeeze the long sides lightly.

steps.title: Rice on, dimple, sides

steps.body_html:
• Lay your right index and middle fingers along the rice and press gently.
  • At the same time curl the left fingers a little so they shape the sides.

steps.title: Press the top

steps.body_html:
• Open your left fingers and roll the piece towards your fingertips so the fish ends up on top, catching it with your right fingers and setting it back in the left palm.
  • (This turn is the kote-gaeshi, the small hand turn.)

steps.title: Turn it over

steps.body_html:
• ① Right thumb and index: pinch the long sides to tighten them.
  • ② Right index and middle: press the fish down onto the rice.
  • ③ Left thumb: nudge the front end square.
  • The left palm stays cupped underneath the whole time.

steps.title: Pinch and press

steps.body_html:
• Turn the piece 180° in your palm and repeat ① ② ③.
  • Two or three rounds in all. On the last press, draw the fish slightly towards you with your right index finger so it lies smooth.

steps.body_html:
• The fish drapes over the top with a little overhang at the ends; the bottom is rounded like a boat; the whole thing is one bite.
  • Serve straight away with soy sauce and ginger. Dip the fish side, not the rice.
